texts.preamble: Suresh Khatri vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 9 January, 2024 High Court Of Chhattisgarh, Bilaspur Order Sheet Cra No. 2269 of 2023 Suresh Khatri Versus State Of Chhattisgarh 09.01.2024
texts.arguments: Learned Counsel appearing for the appellant while inviting attention to the provisions prescribed under sub-section (2) of Section 68 of The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 submits that the Adjudicating Officer, without following the said mandatory provision has passed the order on 14.10.2022 (Annexure A-3) and the appellant has been held liable to pay penalty under Sections 51, 54 and 57 of the Act of 2006 for violation of Section 26 of the said Act and, accordingly, imposed the penalty upon him to the tune of Rs. 8,00,000/- in exercise of the powers enumerated under Section 49 of the said Act. In support, he placed his reliance upon the decision rendered in the matter of Ramakant Gupta vs. State of Chhattisgarh and others, by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in WP(cr) No.220 of 2015. It is contended further that the order as passed by the Adjudicating Officer was affirmed by the Appellate Tribunal and since the order impugned has been passed without following the said mandatory provision, therefore, the effect and operation of the same be kept in abeyance till the disposal of this appeal. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the State/Respondent No.1 has opposed the same and submits that after due examination of the document placed on record, the concerned Adjudicating Officer has passed the said order dated 14.10.2022 and, therefore, the same has rightly been affirmed by the Appellate Tribunal by virtue of its order impugned.
texts.petitioner_arguments: Learned Counsel appearing for the appellant while inviting attention to the provisions prescribed under sub-section (2) of Section 68 of The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 submits that the Adjudicating Officer, without following the said mandatory provision has passed the order on 14.10.2022 (Annexure A-3) and the appellant has been held liable to pay penalty under Sections 51, 54 and 57 of the Act of 2006 for violation of Section 26 of the said Act and, accordingly, imposed the penalty upon him to the tune of Rs. 8,00,000/- in exercise of the powers enumerated under Section 49 of the said Act. In support, he placed his reliance upon the decision rendered in the matter of Ramakant Gupta vs. State of Chhattisgarh and others, by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in WP(cr) No.220 of 2015. It is contended further that the order as passed by the Adjudicating Officer was affirmed by the Appellate Tribunal and since the order impugned has been passed without following the said mandatory provision, therefore, the effect and operation of the same be kept in abeyance till the disposal of this appeal. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the State/Respondent No.1 has opposed the same and submits that after due examination of the document placed on record, the concerned Adjudicating Officer has passed the said order dated 14.10.2022 and, therefore, the same has rightly been affirmed by the Appellate Tribunal by virtue of its order impugned.
